slokas.meaning: One should meditate on Vishnu, dressed in white robes, moon coloured, four-armed, with a cheerful face, for the removal of all obstacles.
The elephant faced one, along with his innumerable attendants, would always remove obstacles, as we depend on Vishvaksena.
I salute Vyasa, the great grandson of Vasishta, the grandson of Shakti, the immaculate son of Parasara, the father of Shukata, the treasure of austerities.

sanskrit: नमो वै ब्रह्मनिधये वासिष्ठाय नमो नमः ॥ ४॥
english: namō vai brahmanidhaye vāsiṣṭhāya namō namaḥ
slokas.meaning: O Vyasa in the form of Vishnu, O Vishnu in the form of Vyasa, O Vasishta, the treasure of the Brahman, I offer my obeisances unto Thee again and again.
Bow I before Vishnu, Who is pure, Who is not affected, Who is permanent, Who is the ultimate truth, and He who wins over all the mortals in this world.
Obeisance to that Vishnu, the all-powerful Vishnu, whose remembrance alone frees one from the bondage of birth and death.
Sri Vaisampayana said: Having heard the Dharma in its entirety and the holy ones in all respects, Yudhisthira again addressed Shantanu.

sanskrit: किमेकं दैवतं लोके किं वाप्येकं परायणम् ।
english: kimekaṁ daivataṁ lōke kiṁ vāpyekaṁ parāyaṇaṁ
slokas.meaning: Yudhishthira asked: Is there one god in this world, or is there one devotee? Whom do men attain to good by praising and worshiping?

sanskrit: को धर्मः सर्वधर्माणां भवतः परमो मतः ।
english: kō dharmaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṁ bhavataḥ paramō mataḥ
slokas.meaning: Which Dharma do you consider to be the supreme of all Dharma? By chanting what is a creature freed from the bondage of birth and death?
Bhishma replied: Praising the Lord of the universe, the God of gods, the infinite Supreme Personality of Godhead, with a thousand names, the man ever rises.
By always worshipping with devotion that imperishable Purusha, meditating on Him, praising Him, bowing down to Him, and performing sacrifices for Him.
By always praising Vishnu, who is without beginning or end, the supreme Lord of all the worlds, and the overseer of the worlds, one goes beyond all sorrows.
The one who is friendly to Brahman, the knower of all dharmas, the increaser of the fame of the worlds, the Lord of the worlds, the great Being, and the source of the existence of all beings.
This, in my opinion, is the greatest of all dharmas: that a person should always worship the lotus-eyed Lord with devotion through hymns of praise.

sanskrit: परमं यो महत्तेजः परमं यो महत्तपः ।
परमं यो महद्ब्रह्म परमं यः परायणम् ॥ १५॥
english: paramaṁ yō mahattejaḥ paramaṁ yō mahattapaḥ
paramaṁ yō mahadbrahma paramaṁ yaḥ parāyaṇam
slokas.meaning: He who is the supreme great Light, He who is the supreme great Penance, He who is the supreme great Brahman, He who is the supreme Goal.

sanskrit: पवित्राणां पवित्रं यो मङ्गलानां च मङ्गलम् ।
दैवतं देवतानां च भूतानां योऽव्ययः पिता ॥ १६॥
english: pavitrāṇāṁ pavitraṁ yō maṅgalānāṁ ca maṅgalam
daivataṁ devatānāṁ ca bhūtānāṁ yō'vyayaḥ pitā
slokas.meaning: He who is the purest of the pure, the most auspicious of the auspicious, the God of gods, and the imperishable Father of all beings.
From whom all beings originate at the beginning of the age, and in whom they again reach dissolution at the end of the age.
Listen, O King, to the thousand names of Vishnu, the chief of the world and Lord of the universe, which are auspicious and remove all sins.
Those secondary names of the great soul which are well-known and sung by the sages, I shall recite for the welfare of all.
The sage of the thousand names is the great sage Veda Vyasa; the meter is Anushtup; the deity is the Lord, the son of Devaki.
The seed is He who is born from the nectar-rayed moon; the power is the son of Devaki; the heart is the chanter of the three Samas; it is used for the sake of peace.
I bow to Vishnu, the victorious, the great Vishnu, the all-powerful, the supreme Lord, the many-formed, the ender of demons, the supreme Purusha.

sanskrit: उद्भवः क्षोभणो देव इति परमो मन्त्रः ।
english: udbhavaḥ kṣobhaṇo deva iti paramo mantraḥ |
slokas.meaning: Of this great mantra of the thousand names of Vishnu, the sage is Veda Vyasa, the meter is Anushtup, the deity is Mahavishnu, the seed is 'born of nectar', the power is 'son of Devaki', the mantra is 'the agitator', the armor is the conch/sword/discus, the weapon is the bow/mace, the eye is the unshakeable wheel-wielder, the heart is the chanter of Samas, the womb is the Bliss of Brahman, the direction-binder is time/seasons, the meditation is the Universal Form. It is used for the pleasure of Lord Mahavishnu.

May Mukunda, with the discus, lotus, mace, and conch in hand, seated on a throne of pearls in the milky ocean, adorned with crystal-like gems, and showered by nectar from white clouds, purify us with joy.

sanskrit: भूः पादौ यस्य नाभिर्वियदसुरनिलश्चन्द्रसूर्यौ च नेत्रे
कर्णावाशाः शिरो द्यौर्मुखमपि दहनो यस्य वास्तेयमब्धिः ।
चित्रं रंरम्यते तं त्रिभुवनवपुषं विष्णुमीशं नमामि ॥ २॥
english: bhūḥ pādau yasya nābhir-viyad-asura-nilaś-candra-sūryau ca netre
karṇāv-āśāḥ śiro dyaur-mukham-api dahano yasya vāstēyam-abdhiḥ
citraṁ raṁramyate taṁ tri-bhuvana-vapuṣaṁ viṣṇum-īśaṁ namāmi
slokas.meaning: I bow to Lord Vishnu, whose body is the three worlds, whose feet are the earth, whose navel is the sky, whose breath is the wind, whose eyes are the sun and moon, whose ears are the directions, whose head is the heavens, whose mouth is fire, and whose stomach is the ocean, within whom the universe of gods, men, and beings plays.

I bow my head to the four-armed Vishnu, who carries the conch and the discus, wears a crown and earrings, is dressed in yellow silks, has eyes like the lotus, and whose chest is adorned with necklaces and the Kaustubha gem.
Seated on a golden throne in the shade of the Parijata tree, is the Lord, dark like the rain-cloud, with large eyes, and beautifully adorned.
I take refuge in Krishna, who has a moon-like face, four arms, a chest marked by Srivatsa, and who is accompanied by Rukmini and Satyabhama.

english: vanamālī gadī śārṅgī śaṅkhī cakrī ca nandakī
slokas.meaning: Adorned with the forest garland, carrying the mace, the bow, the conch, the discus, and the sword; may the illustrious Narayana, the all-pervading Vishnu, the son of Vasudeva, protect us all.

title: PHALASHRUTI — CONCLUDING VERSES
description: The Vishnu Sahasranama, meaning 'Thousand Names of Vishnu,' is a revered hymn in Hinduism that lists the various names and attributes of Lord Vishnu. Each name reflects a different aspect of the deity's nature, qualities, and cosmic functions. The Sahasranama is often recited as a form of devotion and meditation, with each name invoking a specific attribute or blessing associated with Lord Vishnu. It is considered a powerful tool for spiritual growth and connection with the divine.

slokas.meaning: Thus, this thousand divine names of the great-souled Keshava, worthy of being sung, has been recited in its entirety.

sanskrit: नाशुभं प्राप्नुयात् किञ्चित् सोऽमुत्रेह च मानवः ॥ २॥
english: nāśubhaṁ prāpnuyāt kiñcit sō'mutrēha ca mānavaḥ
slokas.meaning: The man who hears this daily or recites it daily will not meet with anything inauspicious in this world or the next.
Parvati asked: By what easy means is the thousand names of Vishnu recited daily by the learned? I wish to hear this, O Lord.

sanskrit: श्रीराम राम रामेति रमे रामे मनोरमे ।
english: śrīrāma rāma rāmēti ramē rāmē manōramē
slokas.meaning: Lord Shiva said: 'Rama, Rama, Rama'—thus I delight in Rama, the captivator of the mind. The name of Rama is equal to the thousand names, O fair-faced one.
